title: EFC — Master Specification (v1 Archive)
description: Canonical master specification for Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), defining the formal structure, notation, and baseline equations for its three coupled base layers: EFC-S (structural/halo layer), EFC-D (energy-flow dynamics), and EFC-C0 (entropy–information capacity mapping). The paper establishes EFC as a thermodynamic information framework that replaces dark matter and dark energy with energy-flow potentials driven by density and entropy gradients.

energy_flow_potential.description: Local energy-flow potential coupling mass density ρ and dimensionless entropy S into a single field. High density with low entropy yields large Ef; high entropy suppresses Ef.

low_entropy_anchor.description: Defines a low-entropy anchor region A where coarse-grained entropy density is much lower than background, serving as a seed for halo formation.

halo_mass_profile.description: Parameterised radial mass density profile for halos with central density ρ₀ and mass scale radius rₛ.

halo_entropy_profile.description: Parameterised dimensionless entropy profile normalised to [0,1] with entropy floor S₀ and entropy core radius rₓ.

information_capacity.description: Baseline EFC-C0 relation mapping entropy to information capacity at fixed density.

mass_density.description: Standard mass density definition used as input to the energy-flow potential.

key_results.main_finding: EFC is formally specified as a three-layer thermodynamic information framework (EFC-S, EFC-D, EFC-C0) with a single central object Ef = ρ(1−S) replacing dark sector components, providing a compact canonical reference for all downstream models, simulations, and epistemic layers.

kill_criteria: KC1: If the energy-flow potential Ef = ρ(1−S) is shown to be mathematically insufficient to reproduce observed galactic rotation curves for any physically reasonable entropy profile S(r).
KC2: If low-entropy anchor regions as defined by ⟨s⟩_A ≪ ⟨s⟩_background are demonstrated not to correlate with observed structure formation sites (galaxy/cluster seeds).

KC3: If the EFC expansion history H(z) derived from flow and entropy gradients is shown to be fundamentally incompatible with observed H(z) data (e.g., BAO, SNe Ia) at >5σ with no viable parameter choice.
KC4: If a rigorous demonstration shows that the entropy–information capacity mapping I(S) ∝ (1−S) leads to internal inconsistencies or violates established thermodynamic bounds.
KC5: If observations require an additional invisible mass/energy component that cannot be absorbed into the (ρ, S) framework under any halo class parameterisation.
